title: ZARA LARSSON RELEASES NEW ALBUM MIDNIGHT SUN

text:
这是一篇发布在 Sony Music Canada 官方网站“Press Release”栏目下的新闻稿，标题为“ZARA LARSSON RELEASES NEW ALBUM MIDNIGHT SUN”，署名主体为 Sony Music Canada，日期为 2025 年 9 月 26 日（Toronto, ON）。文稿宣布并宣传 Zara Larsson 的新专辑《Midnight Sun》，称其为“hotly anticipated”的新作品，通过 Sommer House / Epic Records 在所有数字流媒体平台上发行，并提供智能链接 zaralarsson.lnk.to/MidnightSun 以供收听或购买。稿件将 Zara 描述为“multiplatinum chart-topping global pop powerhouse”，强调她在公众视野近 20 年的艺人生涯。

文中介绍《Midnight Sun》是一张 10 首歌的专辑，被形容为“unapologetically unfiltered and openly vulnerable”，在风格上是“kaleidoscopic pop and euphoric dance”的大胆混合，表达她对自信、脆弱和情绪多面性的呈现。文本称专辑深入探讨 Zara 的艺术之路与成长，展示她“lovestruck, wistful, ambitious, cocky, flippant, and uncertain”等不同面向，凸显情绪张力与艺术成熟度。

新闻稿多次强调发行方为 Sommer House / Epic Records，突出 Zara 作为全球流行歌手的商业成功地位。文中还介绍了一款名为“Midnight Sun (Lisa Frank Edition)”的限量实体 CD，被描述为与 Lisa Frank, Inc. 的“vibrant collaboration”，呈现受粉丝一年间参与的“memes and moments”启发的梦幻水世界视觉主题，并提醒读者在库存耗尽前下单。

稿件同时将专辑与现场演出活动相连接：指出 Zara 接近完成作为嘉宾参与的 Tate McRae“Miss Possessive Tour”体育馆巡演，并在专辑发行日于洛杉矶 Kia Forum 连演两晚。文中引用 Billboard 对她在美国市场前景的乐观评语，并宣布 Zara 自己的“Midnight Sun Tour”，计划秋季自欧洲起跑，北美站定于 2026 年 2 月至 4 月进行，鼓励读者查看其全球巡演行程及官方站点获取更多信息。整体措辞高度宣传性，突出《Midnight Sun》作为 Zara Larsson 个人化程度很高且延续“夏日”意象的第五张录音室专辑，并配合特别版本及巡演进行一体化推广。

text: Rolling Stone’s review by Brittany Spanos presents Zara Larsson’s album Midnight Sun as a high-energy, dance-pop celebration of Scandinavian summer that rarely slows down. The critic emphasizes the album’s unbroken rush of club-ready joy, framed around the concept of a Swedish “Euro summer” with long days and late nights. The review highlights a consistent sonic palette of trance-tinted, glossy electronic pop and narrative lyrics depicting summer romance and sensual imagery. It stresses that the record’s most compelling moments are those that explore messier emotions, such as guilt, anger, and ambition, alongside carefree euphoria. Specific tracks including “Midnight Sun,” “Blue Moon,” “Euro Summer,” “Puss Puss,” “Girl’s Girl,” “Pretty Ugly,” “The Ambition,” and “Saturn’s Return” are discussed as examples of the album’s blend of high-tempo dance-pop and introspective themes. Overall, Spanos assesses the album very positively, calling it a place where Larsson comes into her own, with even formulaic songs shining brighter than a Swedish summer sun and her ambition paying off.

The DIY Magazine review by Otis Robinson, quoted via Album of the Year, characterizes Midnight Sun as nearly nonstop, sun-drenched exuberant pop music. It describes the album as being built on MNEK’s production style and positioned within a Scandi-pop-meets-dance future that Zara Larsson has helped establish. The excerpt suggests a cohesive, high-energy record with continuous brightness and carefully formulated pop structures, and the critic’s 90/100 score reflects a strongly favorable overall assessment, viewing the album as an advanced statement of Larsson’s pop and dance aesthetic.

Beatroutemedia’s review by Atheshan Sureshkumar portrays Midnight Sun as an exemplary modern pop album and an homage to Scandinavian summer. The critic argues that the record is a perfect model of how pop should be made, describing it as a strong, cohesive album with no weak songs, bright and loud production, and heartfelt emotional content. The review highlights the album’s maximalist electro-pop style, unified world of endless daylight and euphoric dance music, and Zara Larsson’s artistic growth through focusing on her authentic sound rather than chasing trends. Numerous tracks are identified as standout moments, including the title track “Midnight Sun,” “Blue Moon,” “Pretty Ugly,” “Girl’s Girl,” “Crush,” “Eurosummer,” and “Hot & Sexy,” each discussed in terms of their sonic character and themes such as messy crushes, emotional chaos, ambition, empowerment, and self-confidence. Overall, the review is emphatically positive, likening the impact of the album’s pop sound to Katy Perry’s Teenage Dream and framing Larsson’s evolution as a journey listeners can feel proud of and connected to.

The Instagram mini-review by marieltalkspop gives a mixed, largely negative personal assessment of Midnight Sun. The reviewer notes limited prior familiarity with Zara Larsson’s discography and states that listening to the album in full for the first time left the impression that it is plain, with songs that mostly sound the same and only a couple standing out. The caption describes the album as forgettable and lacking creativity, framing it as just another release without distinctive elements. The reviewer names “Pretty Ugly” and “Eurosummer” as the only tracks that stood out, while emphasizing that the opinions expressed are subjective.

Album of the Year’s page for Midnight Sun functions as a review aggregator and information hub. It lists the album’s release date as September 26, 2025, and credits labels Sommer House and Epic. The site tags the album under multiple genres, including Dance-Pop, EDM, Baltimore Club, Bubblegum Bass, Contemporary R&B, and Dancefloor Drum and Bass, indicating a multi-genre electronic dance-pop blend. The page includes critic scores and short excerpts from reviews by outlets such as AllMusic and DIY, showing strong critical reception with scores around 80–90 out of 100. Neil Z. Yeung’s AllMusic quote describes the album as short and sweet, a catalog highlight that benefits from its concise length and provides enough of Larsson’s strengths to leave listeners craving more of its blissful sound. The DIY excerpt reiterates that Midnight Sun is near non-stop, sun-drenched, exuberantly formulated pop shaped by MNEK’s production and aligned with a Scandi-pop-meets-dance future that Larsson has paved.

title: "Midnight Sun" Zara Larsson album review
content:
- “Euro summer isn’t over if you don’t want it to be. Zara Larsson’s fifth album, Midnight Sun, is an unbroken rush of high-energy dance-pop joy that refuses to ever slow down.” [4]

- Rolling Stone notes that Larsson is “celebrating the sun-drenched energy of a summer in her home country” and that the album helps keep “the good vibes, long days, and late nights going.” [4]

- On the title track, Rolling Stone writes: “‘Midnight Sun’ is deliriously hypnotic, with notes of trance in its swirling chorus uplifted by Larsson’s extended run.” [4]

- Rolling Stone groups “Blue Moon,” “Euro Summer,” and “Puss Puss” as songs that “traffic in the sweetness,” mentioning “tender scenes of short sundresses, late-night phone calls and handprints left on her ass.” [4]

- Describing “Girl’s Girl,” Rolling Stone notes Larsson “feels guilty for wanting a childhood friend’s man,” and in “Pretty Ugly” she sings over a stomp beat and “threatens slashed tires and crashed cars” while asking, “Have you ever seen a pretty girl get ugly like this?” [4]

- Rolling Stone compares “The Ambition” to “the raw moments of Charli XCX’s Brat,” quoting the lyric: “But that’s the thing with the ambition / I want it so much / Everything’s a competition / So out of touch,” and calling it “one of the biggest earworm moments of the project.” [4]

- On “Saturn’s Return,” Rolling Stone writes that Larsson “leans into life’s confusions, giving up control she sought when she was younger,” highlighting it as a standout. [4]

- Rolling Stone concludes: “Those messier moments are where Larsson comes alive. You can hear her coming into her own across Midnight Sun, where even her more formulaic moments still shine brighter than that Swedish summer sun. That ambition is paying off.” [4]

- DIY’s excerpt via Album of the Year: “Near non-stop, Midnight Sun is entirely sun-drenched, exuberantly formulated pop that's both scaffolded by MNEK's production style and the Scandi-pop-meets-dance future that Zara has readily paved.” [5]

- Beatroutemedia states: “Zara Larsson’s new album isn’t just a regular pop record; it’s a perfect example of how pop music should be made, and I haven’t been this hooked on an album’s sheer, great pop sound since Katy Perry’s Teenage Dream.” [6]

- Beatroutemedia describes the album as “a strong, cohesive record with no weak songs, where every song feels carefully crafted, from the bright, loud production to the genuine, heartfelt feelings at its core.” [6]

- On style, Beatroutemedia writes that Midnight Sun is “an homage to the Scandinavian summer, giving us a vibrant, unified world of endless daylight and euphoric dance music,” and “a fun, maximalist fever dream of electro-pop that never loses sight of its heart.” [6]

- Beatroutemedia on "Midnight Sun" and "Blue Moon": the opening pair is called "pure fire," with the title track offering “soaring vocals over trance-inspired production” and “Blue Moon” delivering “a club-ready beat to celebrate that perfect romantic high.” [6]

- Regarding "Pretty Ugly," Beatroutemedia describes it as “a pure dose of chaotic energy, a rebellious, shouty cheerleader anthem that rejects the idea of being the ‘good girl’ (‘F* the ladylike, more like crazy-like’). It’s empowering, messy fun.” [6]

- On "Girl’s Girl," Beatroutemedia notes that it “brilliantly flips the feminist expectation of female loyalty on its head,” portraying “the horrifying, guilt-ridden feeling of crushing on a friend’s boyfriend.” [6]

- Beatroutemedia calls “Crush” “arguably the highlight of the entire project,” describing it as “an irresistible percussive pop jam with an amazing, show-stopping bridge” that captures “the anxiety and excitement of falling for someone totally wrong for you.” [6]

- For "Eurosummer," Beatroutemedia writes that it is “a total sonic shift,” a “rousing, high-energy dance beat built around hypnotic accordion melodies,” and “the ultimate party track” that “instantly transports you to a dizzying European holiday.” [6]

- Beatroutemedia describes “Hot & Sexy” as “a bold and confident, unavoidable declaration” that opens with “the iconic, commanding sound bite from reality TV legend Tiffany Pollard,” and suggests it cements Zara’s control over the pop scene. [6]

- Beatroutemedia writes that Midnight Sun “proves that when Zara Larsson focuses her immense talent and finds her authentic sound, the result is nothing less than pure, perfect pop,” and that her growth is “a journey we can all be proud of and feel connected to.” [6]

- Marieltalkspop’s caption says: “I found it a little plain; all songs sound the same and only a couple kinda stand out. It’s just one more album to forget about, I couldn’t find anything interesting and I think it lacks creativity.” [7]

- Marieltalkspop notes that "Pretty Ugly" and "Eurosummer" were “the only two songs that stood out to me.” [7]

- Album of the Year lists: “Release Date: September 26, 2025” and labels “Sommer House, Epic” for Zara Larsson – Midnight Sun. [8]

- Album of the Year tags Midnight Sun under genres: Dance-Pop, EDM, Baltimore Club, Bubblegum Bass, Contemporary R&B, Dancefloor Drum and Bass. [8]

- The AllMusic snippet on Album of the Year quotes Neil Z. Yeung: “Short and sweet, this catalog highlight benefits from its length, offering just enough of what Larsson does best to have listeners craving more of this endless bliss.” [8]

- The DIY snippet repeated on Album of the Year reads: “Near non-stop, Midnight Sun is entirely sun-drenched, exuberantly formulated pop that's both scaffolded by MNEK's production style and the Scandi-pop-meets-dance future that Zara has readily paved.” [8]

- Multiple professional reviewers describe Zara Larsson’s album Midnight Sun as near non-stop, sun‑drenched, high‑energy dance‑pop that functions as an homage to Scandinavian/Euro summer, combining exuberant, maximalist electro‑pop production with a cohesive emotional core. [4][5][6][8]

- The production and genre framing of Midnight Sun are widely characterized as dance‑oriented pop built on MNEK’s production style, incorporating elements tagged as Dance‑Pop, EDM, Baltimore Club, Bubblegum Bass, Contemporary R&B, and dancefloor drum and bass. [5][8]

- Critics identify several specific tracks on Midnight Sun as standouts: Beatroutemedia calls "Crush" arguably the highlight of the project, while Rolling Stone singles out "Saturn’s Return" and "The Ambition" for their lyrical focus and emotional or raw quality. [4][6]

- Reviewers from Rolling Stone and Beatroutemedia describe the tracks "Girl’s Girl" and "Pretty Ugly" as exploring messy, morally conflicted or rebellious femininity: guilt over desiring a friend’s partner and rejection of being a "good" or ladylike girl, framing these songs as empowering, chaotic expressions of complex emotions. [4][6]
